title: Cohort-based LTS Compatibility Playbook and Cross-surface Support Specification
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a practical, cohort-driven LTS compatibility playbook that ties runtime, API, SDKs, and console releases to explicit compatibility guarantees and automated upgrade tooling. This ticket specifies the cohort definitions, automated preflight checks, compatibility acceptance criteria, and the gating/rollback policies used during staged rollouts. The goal is to let feature teams and customers understand what combinations of runtime/API/SDK/console are supported, how upgrades are validated, and how automatic fallbacks work when regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable cohort taxonomy (internal dev, early adopters, general availability) with entry/exit criteria documented
A compatibility table mapping runtime semver ranges to supported API versions, SDK minor versions, and console builds (published in Confluence)
Automated preflight validator (compat-checker) that runs smoke tests across runtime+API+SDK+console before canary rollouts
Rollout gate rules implemented in rollout orchestrator (canary size, error budget threshold, latency regressions, token-cost delta) with automated rollback triggers
Upgrade-advisor tool that provides per-customer upgrade guidance and a one-click pin/rollback option in Console
tasks: Define cohort taxonomy and sizing guidance (internal, alpha, beta, GA)
Design compatibility table format and publishing workflow (automated generation from CI)
Implement compat-checker job in CI that runs cross-surface smoke suite and publishes results
Add rollout gates to orchestrator: error-rate, latency-percentile, token-cost-delta, model-fallback-success-rate
Build upgrade-advisor prototype in Console that reads compatibility artifacts and suggests pins or staggered upgrades
Document rollback playbook and create runbook snippets for on-call
Integrate version fingerprinting in SDKs and runtime for fast mismatch detection in logs
decisions: Adopt cohorting (internal -> alpha -> beta -> GA) instead of binary canary-only approach to increase observational surface
Compat-checker will be the canonical source for compatibility assertions; results are stored as artifacts and referenced in release notes
Semantic versioning mapping: runtime major bumps may require SDK minor bump; minor runtime bumps must remain backward-compatible across pinned API shims
Console will support per-organization pin overrides to hold customers on a known-good combination for up to the LTS window
rollout_gates: Canary: 0.5% traffic for 60m with zero critical errors and <=10% increase in p95 latency
Alpha cohort: 2% traffic for 24h with automated regressions checks and manual review signoff
Beta cohort: 20% traffic for 72h with extended quality tests and customer opt-in invitations
GA: progressive ramp after 7 days of beta stability or explicit release approval
Automatic rollback triggers: error rate increase > 300% baseline, p99 latency increase > 200ms, token-cost increase > 15% without quality improvement
upgrade_tooling_requirements: compat-checker CLI that runs the canonical smoke suite locally or in CI and emits a pass/fail artifact
upgrade-advisor backend that queries compatibility artifacts and produces per-customer upgrade timelines
Console UI that surfaces recommended pins, current compatibility health, and one-click pin/unpin actions
SDK helper libraries that detect runtime/API mismatches and surface actionable telemetry to the Console
observability_requirements: Per-version telemetry: request latency distributions, error classification, token cost per model variant
Release-correlated dashboards that show cohort-level metrics (by canary/alpha/beta/GA)
Automatic anomaly detection alerts tied to rollout gates and integrated with on-call escalation
Post-release regression report generated 24h after each cohort stage summarizing pass/fail of key checks
risks: Undetected cross-surface incompatibilities: SDKs or Console may surface bugs not covered by runtime smoke tests
Overly strict gates causing release delays and customer churn for minor changes
Insufficient telemetry granularity for small-cohort rollouts leading to noisy signals
Operational complexity of supporting many pinned permutations for long periods (support burden)
mitigations: Expand smoke suite to include representative SDK and Console flows; add fuzz inputs for edge cases
Tune gate thresholds after first three rollouts using historical data and make them configurable per-release
Introduce cohort sampling rules that prioritize high-risk customers for early validation
Define pinning SLA and automatic cleanup policy (e.g., pin expiration after 90 days unless extended by Support)
notes: This ticket focuses on the playbook and tooling spec; implementation will be split into multiple engineering tickets for compat-checker, orchestrator gates, and Console features
Align with Security on any compatibility artifacts that leak internal build metadata before public release
Coordinate with Developer Experience for SDK fingerprinting changes to ensure minimal churn for third-party integrations
